This Sprinter Camper Van Breaks the Mold With a Rear Bathroom and a Manual Elevator Bed
15 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion
Today's featured build is based on a Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase. It was created earlier this year by the Auburn, California-based AdventureBumss. This company specializes in handcrafted homes on wheels that are designed to fit the needs of each customer.
This conversion was a partial build, in the sense that the customer provided the Sprinter which already had some work done, such as the floors and some cabinetry. Before we check out the inside, let me shortly mention some important exterior upgrades.
For starters, the Sprinter rides on alloy wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires. Next, at the front, you'll come across a massive Backwoods Adventure Mods bumper complete with an LED light bar and a winch. On the opposite end, there's a spare tire carrier attached to the driver-side door.
On top of the vehicle, the builders added a rack that holds a front-facing LED light bar and solar panels.
Other notable mods are side steps and power and water connections. The van came with two windows already installed, and AdventureBumss added three more windows: one on the side and two at the back.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion Stepping inside, you'll be greeted by a warm and roomy interior. It has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van and used after you set up camp.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for a cohesive design with a slatted pine ceiling, wall panels and cabinetry with a raw wood look, and wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring. The look is complemented by white Corian solid surface countertops and brown leather drawer handles.
Above, you'll find the main sleeping arrangement. It's an elevator bed system that's much more primitive than the elevator beds we've seen in other camper vans.
Instead of having an electronically controlled system, this bed has two tow straps on each corner: one to lower and raise the bed and the other to stabilize it. They hook into factory D-rings or installed D-rings.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion Dead ahead of the entrance, you'll come across a simple seating area comprising a bench with a Lagun table. The bench is so long that it could double as a narrow bed.
Next, we have the kitchen, which is split into two units, one on each side of the living space. It features a fridge with a tiny freezer compartment and a copper sink with a pull-out tap and a filtered water faucet.
There's an abundant amount of counter space available - I can't imagine a meal so complicated that would require even more surface area.
Three overhead cabinets, several drawers, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage in the kitchen. The latter houses a freshwater tank, an electric water heater, a pump, and a water filtration system.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion There's also a floor-to-ceiling unit on the driver side integrating a hanging closet and three drawers. Above it, the builders added a ceiling A/C unit.
Interestingly, the rear part of the interior is where you'll discover the bathroom and the garage. I said "interestingly" because few camper vans come with rear bathrooms.
The shower is integrated into a panel sitting on the side of the hallway - basically, you can wash yourself right in the middle of this part of the van and use a curtain to separate the area from the rest of the living space.
The water drains into a floor-integrated stainless steel pan, which then routes it to an under-mounted greywater tank. Moreover, a Maxxair vent fan above will draw out the moisture produced by showering.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion Opposite the shower, the builders fitted a small counter and two drawers. The larger drawer accommodates a portable toilet.
Finally, the garage sits on the driver's side, behind the panel holding the shower. It's accessible only from the back of the van, after opening the door on the left.
We don't know the specs of the power system inside this rig. However, based on other AdventureBumss creations, I'd assume that it's packing a 200 Ah lithium battery paired with a 3,000 W inverter.
The garage offers a decent amount of storage space. It has an open storage compartment that's about half of the interior height, as well as three drawers. You also get some charging points if you need to charge your gadgets.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion The "command center" for the rig's utilities is integrated into the driver-side kitchen wall panel. It includes two standard outlets, a thermostat for the heater, two USB plugs, a battery monitor, an inverter controller, and a light switch.
All in all, this custom creation by Adventure Bumss packs all the essentials needed to hit the road in comfort. It's clear that a lot of work went into bringing the customer's vision to life, and I'm sure they were really happy with the result.
